question: Pallavi bought a toy for ₹255, decorated it at a cost of ₹5 and sold the toy for ₹154. Find the loss or profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP = Purchase price + Overhead cost = ₹255 + ₹5 = ₹260

SP = ₹154

Loss = Total CP − SP = 260 − 154 = ₹106

Loss % = (Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

Loss % = (106 ÷ 260) × 100 = 530/13% loss

**∴ The correct answer is 530/13% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Purchase price of the toy = ₹255

Cost of decoration (overhead) = ₹5

Selling price (SP) = ₹154

 
 Total CP = ₹260
 
 
 SP = ₹154
 
 

 Loss = ₹106
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 Loss % = (106 ÷ 260) × 100 = 530/13%

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = Purchase Price + Overhead Charges

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 255 + 5 = ₹260

⇒ Since CP is greater than SP, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = Total CP − SP

⇒ Loss = 260 − 154 = ₹106

⇒ Loss % = (106 ÷ 260) × 100

⇒ Loss % = (53 ÷ 130) × 100

⇒ Loss % = (53 ÷ 13) × 10

⇒ Loss % = 530/13%

**∴ The correct answer is 530/13% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentages

Profit or Loss percentages are always calculated on the Total Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Overhead Charges

Any additional expenses like transportation, repair, or decoration are added to the purchase price to calculate the Total CP.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Final SP = MP − Discount.
